page.title: The visualization house — principles
page.subtitle: how every output of the engine becomes a finalized, reusable figure
page.reads: This is the right-side companion to the method + library principles. The drawers tell you what each step IS; this page tells you how each step's OUTPUT gets drawn, once, and reused everywhere.

the_model.note: One idea, borrowed straight from the drawers: separate the data from how it is drawn.

points.name: A viz is a render-from-data block
points.body: block = render(data). The figure never hard-codes its numbers; it fetches its data file and draws it. Fix the generator, never the deployed figure (the same contract the method-engine drawers obey).

points.name: Finalize once, reuse everywhere
points.body: Each block is locked in ONE place — the visualization house (the gallery / pattern-book). The reading room does not re-build figures; it composes the locked blocks.

points.name: The reading room is a grid of blocks
points.body: Composition is CSS grid: each block is a cell. That gives editorial freedom — arrange the room like a magazine, drop in [ tributary, public ] where you want it, leave a placeholder that fills itself from data.

points.name: Headless, so the backend can change under it
points.body: Because data and render are decoupled, reading-SB can improve the data (a smarter export, a new field) without touching the figure, and design-SB can re-skin the figure without touching the data.

points.name: Each block self-documents (a spec drawer, coming)
points.body: Every figure will carry its own drawer — its data source, the method-engine node it visualizes, its encoding (what each colour / shape / opacity means), and the design rationale — the same way each method-engine node has a drawer. So a new LLM can read the spec and re-render the figure into a totally different frontend (a future reading room, unlike today's). The figure is portable because its spec is explicit, not baked into one page. On the gallery, every block already names the method-engine node it draws and the data file behind it.

two_axes.note: Every block is located on two independent axes. The first is structure (the menu); the second is framing (a lens toggle on the SAME block).

axes.body: How far the figure sits from the raw encoding. ENCODED = drawn straight from the coded data (one per thing the bowtie collects). ANALYZED = needs a further analysis pass (gloss). SOURCED = needs texts/images pulled from the library (canon, compare, partiture, the Sitz context). SYNTHESIS = remixes two prior outputs into a third.

The same block, two skins. ACADEMIC (for the thesis / a professor): the encoding made auditable — counts, certainty, the seam, 'lines are proposals, not proof of dependence'. PUBLIC (for a seeker diving into wisdom texts): the invitation — the finding, the story, the contemplative read, apparatus tucked away. Same data, same block; the academic view shows the researcher the encoding, the public view shows the reader the meaning. (This is the METHOD-vs-research-view split from the drawers, at figure scale.)

the_process.note: One store, one file, one owner per file, two roles working in tandem — no copies, no scattered files. The seamless pipeline.
steps: The DB is the single store of record (CLAUDE.md §2.13). The method-engine drawers name the exact tables a figure draws from (passages · source_move · connect_edge · lineage_record). No figure ever hand-authors data.

reading/method SB OWNS every DB-derived data feed. A regenerable export reads the DB and writes the feed DIRECTLY into the served location (engine/data/) — one file, committed by the data side, never hand-edited, re-run to refresh. This is the headless backend: the frontend fetches this file, nothing is copied.

design-SB OWNS the render + design content: the .html / .js, and any render-config it authors (the diagram structure, this principles doc). design-SB never writes a DB-derived data file. The line is: if it is regenerable from the DB it is reading/method SB's; if it is design/render, it is design-SB's.
the PI reviews on the LIVE figure (never a markdown mock).
a Cold Read / crit pass on the rendered figure; fixes fold back into the DATA (reading/method SB re-runs the export) or the RENDER (design-SB), each to its owner.
Result: one file per output, owned by the data side, rendered by the frontend side, in one repo. Headless, no copies, no 'which json is right?'.

signature_look.note: One skeleton, one skin — a signature visualization look, so the whole gallery reads as one instrument.
rules: One palette, one type family across every figure (the GoM house: warm-white ground / night skin, fern·moss·terracotta·honey·olive, Newsreader + Inter + IBM Plex Mono). Never two palettes in parallel.
Derived from the two house patterns (HOUSE_PATTERN, reading_room_house_pattern) and from spine.html — the reference for what a finished GoM figure feels like.
Negative space is first-class: a figure shows what was NOT coded (hollow marks) as clearly as what was — the LACUNA stance at figure scale.
The academic skin is the source of truth; the public skin is a re-frame of it (and can be run through Lovable for extra warmth), never a different figure.
Every figure carries its honest caption: what the marks mean, and what they do NOT claim.

roadmap.note: The redesign queue — every output, its raw-material predecessor, and where it is. Worked one block at a time; the historical artifacts are the material to redesign FROM, not the destination.
